summary.one_liner: A tiny, educational JavaScript interpreter written in JavaScript that demonstrates closures by interpreting a small subset of the language.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes an interpreter for a small subset of JavaScript, written in JavaScript, meant to explain closures. Supported syntax includes numeric, boolean, null and undefined literals, identifiers, binary operators (+, -, *, /, ==, ===, !=, !==, and >=), unary ! and -, and the ternary conditional. It also supports arrow function expressions, call expressions, and const variable declarations. The README says assignment and the traditional function keyword are not implemented, and that const bindings behave like letrec. The goal is readable code rather than spec compliance or speed. The README says the project is a work in progress and points to its unit tests.
use_cases: studying how an interpreter is built
experimenting with a subset of JavaScript semantics
notable: Written in JavaScript so the interpreter itself is easy to read
Arrow functions only; no traditional function syntax
Only const declarations; no assignment or mutation
Const declarations behave like letrec, allowing recursion such as the factorial example
caveats: Work in progress according to the README
Not spec-compliant and not optimized for speed, by design
Supports only a tiny subset of JavaScript; no assignment, no function keyword, and only const
